newsitem.title: USA: CFM says adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: CFM says adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: CFM Technologies Inc directors said Friday they adopted a shareholder rights plan.

The company said the plan is similar to those adopted by a number of other companies following favorable rulings by courts in various jurisdictions. CFM said is not aware of any intent on the part of any potential acquirer to commence a bid for control of the company.
The company said the rights will have no dilutive effect, will not affect reported earnings per share and will not change the way in which CFM's shares are traded.
Terms provide for a dividend distribution of one right for each share of common stock of CFM to holders of record at the close of business on May 9, 1997.

The rights would become exercisable if an acquiring party accumulated, or announced an offer to acquire, 20 percent or more of CFM's common stock. The rights would expire on April 24, 2007. Each right would entitle the holder to buy one one-hundredth of a share of a new series of preferred stock at a price of $180.
In addition, the company said, upon the occurrence of certain events, holders of the rights will be entitled to purchase either CFM stock or shares in an "acquiring entity" at half of market value.
CFM will generally be entitled to redeem the rights at $.001 per right at any time until the 10th day following the acquisition of 20 percent of its common stock.
